about: Olympus is a Japanese maker of medical endoscopes, surgical devices and life science microscopes, headquartered in Tokyo, which exited the consumer camera business in 2021 (sold to OM Digital Solutions). Customers are hospitals and laboratories in over 100 countries. Founded in 1919, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (7733). Legacy consumer brand through cameras, now mainly a healthcare B2B brand.

NJOY is a US maker of vaping products, with pod-based e-cigarettes such as NJOY Ace and Daily, based in Richmond, Virginia. Altria acquired NJOY in 2023 for about $2.75 billion. It was among the first FDA-authorised vaping brands, but lost key patent litigation to Juul in 2023. Nicotine product with strict marketing limits, so sponsorship suitability is doubtful.

Chint Electrics is the Zhejiang-based unit of Chint Group, one of China's largest makers of low-voltage electrical equipment such as circuit breakers, contactors, relays, meters and transformers. Based in Yueqing, near Wenzhou. Customers are utilities, builders, industry and distributors in more than 100 countries. Listed in Shanghai (601877). Mainly B2B, though the group has solar and energy storage units and sponsorship activity.

Humane was a US consumer hardware startup, based in San Francisco, founded by former Apple executives Bethany Bongiorno and Imran Chaudhri, which launched the AI Pin, a wearable AI assistant, in 2024 to poor reviews. HP acquired its assets and team in 2025 for about $116 million and the Pin was discontinued. Not an active sponsor prospect.

Swappie is a Finnish online marketplace and refurbisher of used smartphones, mainly iPhones, with refurbished devices sold with a warranty in Europe and expanding into the US. Based in Helsinki, it was founded in 2016 and raised about $188 million. Customers are consumers. Mainly online, a fast-growing consumer brand in Finland and the Nordics.

Yuze Semiconductor is a research and development company in the consumer electronics sector, according to Crunchbase, based in Yunnan, China. Funding shown is CNY 1.2 million. Its products, customers and ownership are not stated in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Key Tronic is a US electronics manufacturing services provider, based in Spokane Valley, Washington, building keyboards, controls and other electronic and plastic products for industrial, medical and consumer brand customers from plants in the US, Mexico, Vietnam and China. Founded in 1969, it has revenue of about $600 million. Listed on Nasdaq (KTCC). B2B contract manufacturer with no consumer profile.

Cellularline is an Italian maker of smartphone and tablet accessories, such as cases, chargers and headsets, based in Reggio Emilia, selling through electronics retailers in Europe under the Cellularline, Interphone (motorbike helmets intercoms) and MusicSound brands. Listed on Borsa Italiana (CELL). Consumer-facing brand with a strong presence in Italian retail, and a link to motorcycling.

New Vision Electronics is described by Crunchbase as a company in automotive and electronics, based in Stuttgart, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany, and marked as listed. About $55.8 million of funding is shown. The input does not give products, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chipone Technology is a Beijing-based Chinese integrated circuit design company, working on chips for display drivers and mobile devices, and related power and driver ICs. Its products serve Chinese smartphone and display panel manufacturers. Founded in 2008, it has listed on the Shanghai STAR Market in 2023 (688593). Funding of around 6.5 billion yuan is shown. B2B semiconductor supplier with no consumer brand visibility.

about: Ampere Computing is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2017 by Renee James, developing Arm-based server processors (Altra, AmpereOne) for cloud and data centre workloads. Customers include Oracle, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Tencent, and Ampere emphasizes power efficiency. Based in Santa Clara, California. Oracle held a significant stake, and in 2025 SoftBank agreed to acquire it for about 6.5 billion dollars. B2B chip designer with no consumer brand visibility.

Velodyne Lidar was a San Jose, California-based maker of lidar sensors used in autonomous vehicles, driver assistance, robotics and mapping, founded by David Hall (who also founded Velodyne Acoustics). It went public in 2020 via a SPAC with Graf Industrial (Nasdaq: VLDR). In 2023 it merged with rival Ouster in an all-stock deal, and the combined company continues as Ouster. Customers were automakers, robotaxi and industrial firms. B2B sensor brand; limited consumer awareness.

Venustech (Venus Information Technology) is a Chinese cybersecurity company, headquartered in Beijing and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002439), selling network security products and services such as firewalls, intrusion detection, security management and consulting to telecom operators, government and large enterprises. Founded in 1996 and one of China's established security vendors with thousands of staff. State-related and enterprise customers dominate. B2B technology brand with no consumer visibility.

Pragmatic Semiconductor is a UK company in Cambridge that makes ultra-low-cost flexible integrated circuits on thin plastic-like substrates, using thin-film transistor technology rather than silicon. These chips target packaging, healthcare, wearables and IoT items where cost matters. Founded in 2010 as a spin-out of Cambridge University and Plastic Logic, with its fab at Sedgefield, County Durham, it has raised around 400 million dollars from Cambridge Innovation Capital and UK government sources. B2B component maker with no consumer brand.

Dresser Utility Solutions is a Houston company providing metering, measurement and flow solutions, including gas meters, regulators and valves, for natural gas utilities and industrial customers. It operated as part of the Dresser group and is described in the input as a provider of metering products. Funding of about 335 million dollars is shown. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Koncar is a Croatian electrical engineering group headquartered in Zagreb, producing power transformers, electric locomotives and trams (Zagreb's Crotram), generators, switchgear, and energy and rail electronics, with exports to Europe and elsewhere. It has about 4,000 employees and revenue of several hundred million euros, and is listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange (KOEI). Well-known industrial name in Croatia and the region, with some sports sponsorship. B2B energy and transport technology.

Quantum Delta NL is a Dutch public-private programme and partnership, with its centre in Delft, that coordinates research and industry in quantum technology across the Netherlands, funded by the National Growth Fund with around 615 million euros from the government. It supports quantum computing, sensing and communication and links universities such as TU Delft and Leiden with companies. Not a commercial company with customers. Public-sector research brand with low consumer awareness.

about: SkyWater Technology is a US semiconductor foundry and engineering services company, a Department of Defense Trusted Foundry, based in Bloomington, Minnesota, with fabs in Minnesota and Florida. It manufactures chips for aerospace and defence, medical, automotive, industrial and quantum computing customers, including technology development services. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (SKYT) and acquired Infineon's Austin fab in 2025. Revenue is around 300 million dollars. B2B and government supplier with no consumer brand.

XMC (Wuhan Xinxin Semiconductor Manufacturing) is a Chinese memory and logic chip foundry in Wuhan, Hubei, founded in 2006 and a major subsidiary of Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) group. It manufactures 3D NAND flash, DRAM and other chips and provides foundry services. Its shareholders include Chinese state funds. Funding is shown in yuan (about 2.7 billion). B2B semiconductor business with no consumer visibility, although the YMTC brand features in storage devices.

Black Semiconductor is a German deep-tech company based in Aachen, developing graphene-based photonic chips that combine optical connectivity with silicon, for AI data centres and high-performance computing. Founded in 2020 by Daniel Schall as a spin-out of the AMO research centre, it received substantial support from the EU's IPCEI programme and German government funding, plus private investors. Funding of about 265 million is shown. B2B technology with no consumer awareness.

about: Hemlock Semiconductor Operations is a Michigan-based manufacturer of polycrystalline silicon for the semiconductor and solar industries, with its main plant at Hemlock, Michigan and a Clarksville, Tennessee site. It is majority owned by Dow, with Corning and Shin-Etsu as minority shareholders. It supplies chipmakers and solar wafer producers worldwide, and has secured CHIPS Act-related support. B2B materials supplier with low public brand awareness.

Red Electrica de Espana (Redeia) is the Spanish transmission system operator, owning and operating the high-voltage electricity grid and managing the national power system, and it also operates fibre networks (Reintel) and satellite businesses (Hispasat). Headquartered in Alcobendas, Madrid, it is listed on the Spanish stock exchange (RED, Ibex 35), with the Spanish state holding 20 percent via SEPI. Revenue is around 2 billion euros. Regulated B2B utility with a public profile in Spain, particularly after the April 2025 blackout.

Keenon Robotics is a Shanghai-based maker of service robots, particularly delivery robots for restaurants and hotels, including the Dinerbot and Bellabot, and healthcare and cleaning robots. Founded in 2010 by Li Tong, it sells to restaurants, hotels and hospitals in over 60 countries, and is backed by Meituan, Matrix Partners and Sequoia China. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO. Funding is about 229 million dollars. B2B hardware brand with visibility in restaurants.

QuEra Computing is a Boston-based quantum computing company, founded in 2018 as a spin-out from Harvard and MIT research (Mikhail Lukin, Vladan Vuletic, Markus Greiner), building neutral-atom quantum computers and offering access through Amazon Braket and its own systems. It raised about 247 million dollars, including investment from Google, SoftBank, Nvidia and Valor Equity Partners. Customers are research institutions and government labs. B2B deep-tech brand with niche profile.

Empower Semiconductor is a Milpitas, California chip company developing integrated voltage regulators and power-management chips, notably its Crescendo product that shrinks and speeds up power delivery for AI accelerators, data centres and high-performance computing. Customers are chip designers and server and AI-hardware makers, with revenue from semiconductor sales. Founded in 2017, it raised about $140 million in 2025 and over $200 million in total. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

about: GlobalWafers is a Taiwan-listed maker of silicon wafers, the base material for semiconductors, supplying chipmakers worldwide with polished, epitaxial and SOI wafers plus silicon carbide wafers. It acquired the US wafer maker MEMC (formerly SunEdison Semiconductor), whose operations are in Saint Peters, Missouri, shown as the location here, and has expanded in Texas with US CHIPS Act support. One of the top four wafer suppliers globally. B2B materials supplier with little public brand awareness.

about: Guzman Energy is a Denver-based wholesale power provider and energy developer in the western US, selling electricity to rural electric cooperatives and municipal utilities and developing solar, wind and storage projects, including a deal to acquire coal-plant assets and transition them to renewables. Founded in 2016 by Rob Guzman, it has raised around $210 million in financing. Revenue comes from wholesale power sales. B2B utility business with limited public brand awareness. Funding shown is mainly project and growth capital.

about: Remixpoint is a Japanese company, listed in Tokyo (ticker 3825), that describes itself as an electric services firm. Its business centres on retail electricity supply, power trading and energy services, with additional recent activity in cryptocurrency holdings and used-car/e-commerce ventures. It has issued capital shown here as 31.5 billion yen in funding. Moderate profile in Japan's small-cap market, with little consumer brand awareness internationally. Details beyond the electricity business are not confirmed.

about: TELUS Health is the health technology division of Canadian telecom group TELUS, offering electronic medical records, pharmacy and claims-management software, virtual care, and employee wellbeing and assistance services (including the former LifeWorks business) to employers, insurers, clinics and governments. It serves hundreds of millions of people worldwide and is based in Vancouver. TELUS itself is listed on the TSX and NYSE as T and TU. B2B and B2B2C healthcare brand; moderate recognition in Canada.

Blackline Safety is a Calgary company making connected gas detectors and wearable devices (G7 and G6 monitors) that alert safety teams to gas exposure, falls and emergencies, plus cloud software for tracking workers. Customers are oil and gas, utilities, chemicals, mining and construction firms, paid through hardware and subscriptions. Listed on the Toronto exchange as BLN, it was founded in 2004 and operates in about 100 countries. B2B industrial safety brand with limited consumer awareness.

Lumafield is a San Francisco hardware and software company that makes Neptune, an affordable industrial CT scanner, plus Voyager analysis software, letting engineers look inside parts and products to inspect quality and find defects. Customers include manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, medical devices and consumer goods. Founded in 2019 by veterans of Mars and other firms, it raised about $67 million in 2025, bringing funding to roughly $190 million. B2B industrial technology with little consumer awareness.

Marvel Fusion is a Munich-based developer of laser-driven fusion energy technology, using nanostructured targets and ultra-short, high-power lasers to aim for commercial fusion power. Founded in 2019, it has raised a Series B of about 113 million euros in 2025 and is building laser facilities with Colorado State University in the US. Funding shown is around 165 million. Revenue is minimal, since it is pre-commercial research-stage. Deep-tech energy company with little consumer brand awareness.

R2 is a Mexico City embedded lending platform that offers capital and credit tools to businesses through partner platforms, plus corporate lending. It has raised about $180 million in a mix of equity and debt. Customers are merchants and fintech platforms in Latin America. B2B finance with low public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Swimlane is a Denver security automation company that sells a low-code platform for security orchestration, automation and response, which helps security teams respond to alerts faster using AI. Customers are large enterprises and government agencies, paid by software subscriptions. Founded in 2014, it raised a $45 million round in 2025, bringing funding to about $182 million. B2B cybersecurity with little consumer awareness.

VitalHub is a Toronto-listed healthcare software company (TSX: VHI) providing electronic patient records, case management, patient flow and mobile tools to health systems and mental health providers, chiefly in the UK (NHS) and Canada. Revenue is from software licences and subscriptions, and it grows through acquisitions. Funding is shown as around 270 million Canadian dollars. B2B healthcare IT with little consumer brand awareness.

Figment is a Toronto-based provider of institutional-grade staking and blockchain infrastructure, running validator nodes and wallet APIs for proof-of-stake networks such as Ethereum, Solana and Cosmos for exchanges, funds and wallets. Revenue comes from a share of staking rewards and fees. Founded in 2018, it has raised about $164 million, including a Series C. B2B crypto infrastructure with limited mainstream consumer awareness.

loxus develops, manufactures and commercialises industrial and energy equipment, based in Oneonta, New York, with products in electronics and energy. Crunchbase shows funding of about $164 million. Beyond that, the company's customers, scale and products are not clearly known. It appears to be a B2B industrial technology business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Veradigm, formerly Allscripts, is a Chicago-based healthcare technology company selling electronic health records, practice management and data analytics products to physician practices, hospitals and life-sciences firms, including the Practice Fusion and Payer Solutions lines. It was delisted from Nasdaq after delayed financial filings and was taken private in 2025 by Rob Cohen's Allscripts-related investors; the Crunchbase funding is about $175 million. B2B healthcare IT with limited consumer awareness.

The company serves device makers and telecom customers in China. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness. Further details, ownership and scale were not confirmed. about: Connecteam is a New York-based, Israeli-founded multi-functional workforce management app for frontline and deskless employees, combining scheduling, time tracking, task management, internal communication and training, sold by monthly subscription. Founded in 2014, it raised a $120 million round in 2024 from Spectrum Equity, bringing funding to about $158 million. Customers are small and medium businesses across industries. B2B software with limited consumer awareness.

Xinsheng Semiconductor is a semiconductor research and manufacturing company based in Futian, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. Crunchbase lists funding of about 1.1 billion yuan. Its specific products, customers, ownership and scale are not detailed in the input. It would be a B2B component business with no consumer brand awareness. Based in Helsinki, it is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki. Funding of about 190 million is shown. Customers are workshops and parts retailers. B2B distributor with little consumer awareness.

about: XCENA is a Seongnam, South Korea based fabless semiconductor company that develops data-centric chips, notably memory-based computational storage using the CXL interface for AI and data centre workloads. Founded in 2022, it has raised about $186 million. Customers are cloud providers and server makers, and revenue would come from chip and module sales. B2B chip developer with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Altair Semiconductor is an Israeli fabless chip company, based in Hod Hasharon, which developed LTE chipsets for mobile and Internet of Things devices. It was acquired by Sony in 2016 for about $212 million and became part of Sony Semiconductor Israel. Customers were device and module makers. Funding of about $174 million is shown. B2B component maker with no consumer brand awareness.

NKT is a Copenhagen-based Danish cable and accessories maker, specialising in high-voltage power cables, including subsea cables for offshore wind and interconnectors, plus medium- and low-voltage cables and accessories. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen under NKT, with revenue of around 3 billion euros. Customers are grid operators, wind developers and utilities. B2B manufacturer with little consumer brand awareness.

Weebit Nano is an Australian-listed (ASX: WBT) semiconductor IP company, with its operations in Hod Hasharon, Israel, developing resistive RAM (ReRAM) non-volatile memory technology licensed to chip foundries and manufacturers for use in embedded applications. Customers are chipmakers like SkyWater, GlobalFoundries and onsemi. Revenue is from licence fees and royalties. Funding of about $177 million is shown. B2B technology with no consumer brand awareness.

Digimarc is a Beaverton, Oregon software company offering digital watermarking and product authentication, helping brands, retailers and packagers embed invisible identifiers in packaging, print and media for traceability, recycling, counterfeit protection and digital rights. Customers include consumer goods companies and government agencies such as central banks. It is listed on Nasdaq (DMRC) and was founded in 1995. Mostly B2B technology, so public brand awareness is low.

Horizon Quantum is a Singapore quantum computing software company building tools that let developers write programs for quantum and classical hardware, plus its own quantum hardware testbed. Customers are enterprises, research institutions and developers. It went public in 2026 through a SPAC merger with dMY Squared Technology Group, giving a listing on Nasdaq. Total funding shown is about 131 million dollars. It is a specialist B2B deep-tech brand with little consumer recognition.

Kopin is a Westborough, Massachusetts maker of microdisplays and optics, including OLED and micro-LED screens, for military night vision and thermal sights, augmented and virtual reality headsets, and avionics. Customers are defence primes and the US military and consumer-electronics makers. Founded in 1984, it trades on Nasdaq (KOPN). B2B component supplier with low consumer brand awareness. Revenue comes from product sales and development contracts, mainly with defence customers. Consumer awareness of the brand is low because it supplies other manufacturers rather than selling directly to the public.

Kromek Group is a Sedgefield, County Durham maker of radiation detection and imaging products based on cadmium zinc telluride semiconductor technology, used in medical imaging, nuclear security and CBRN threat detection, plus analytical instruments. Customers include hospitals, imaging manufacturers and homeland security agencies. It trades on London's AIM market (KMK). It is a B2B instrument supplier with little consumer awareness.

Laser Photonics is an Orlando, Florida maker of industrial laser cleaning systems used to remove rust, paint and coatings from metal surfaces, along with laser marking and related equipment. Customers are manufacturers, aerospace, automotive and defence contractors. It listed on Nasdaq (LASE) in 2022 and is a small company. It is a B2B equipment brand with little awareness among consumers.

MaxLinear is a Carlsbad, California fabless semiconductor company making broadband, connectivity, infrastructure and industrial chips, including cable and fibre access, Wi-Fi, Ethernet and optical interconnect parts for data centres. Customers are equipment makers such as network and device manufacturers. Founded in 2003, it trades on Nasdaq (MXL). Its attempted 2023 acquisition by Silicon Motion was terminated. It is B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

SCHMID Group is a Freudenstadt, Germany equipment maker producing wet-process machines and systems for printed circuit boards, semiconductors, solar cells and energy storage technology. Customers are electronics and solar manufacturers in Asia, Europe and the US. It listed on Nasdaq (SHMD) through a SPAC merger in 2024. B2B capital equipment, little consumer brand awareness. Revenue comes from large equipment orders, which makes sales cyclical. The brand is little known outside its industry, and there is no consumer-facing marketing.

Zapata Quantum (formerly Zapata Computing) is a Boston company that built enterprise quantum and AI software including the Orquestra platform to run industrial and financial workloads. Customers included large banks and industrial firms. It went public through a SPAC in 2024, then ceased operations in October 2024. The company is effectively defunct and not a viable sponsor. At its 2024 listing it was one of the better-known quantum software names, but the shutdown means it is no longer an active prospect.

Aehr Test Systems is a Fremont, California maker of test and burn-in equipment for semiconductors, including systems that test silicon carbide power devices, photonics and AI processors at wafer or package level. Customers are chipmakers and automotive and data centre suppliers. It trades on Nasdaq (AEHR) and was founded in 1977. B2B, little consumer brand awareness. Revenue comes from system sales, which move with chip industry spending cycles, and from service contracts. It has no consumer brand and little public profile outside the semiconductor industry.

Raspberry Pi is a Cambridge, UK maker of low-cost credit-card-sized single-board computers, the Raspberry Pi 5, Pico microcontrollers and related hardware, used by hobbyists, schools and industrial customers worldwide, with over 60 million units sold. It earns from hardware sales. It listed on the London Stock Exchange in June 2024 (RPI) and has ties to the Raspberry Pi Foundation. A well-known technology and education brand among makers, with engineering links to Formula 1 team technology programmes in the UK.

SKYX Platforms is a Florida-based smart home technology company, formerly SQL Technologies, selling plug-and-play ceiling fixtures and a patented ceiling socket system that allows lights and fans to be installed without wiring, along with e-commerce brands Belami and Lighting. Customers are homeowners, builders and retailers. It is listed on Nasdaq (SKYX). Its branding is small but growing in lighting. Revenue comes from lighting and fan sales through its own websites and retail partners, with the plug-and-play system still being rolled out to builders. It is a small company with growing but limited consumer visibility.

SmartKem is a Manchester, UK and Wilmington-based maker of organic thin-film transistor materials for displays, especially micro-LED and flexible electronics, with a patented organic semiconductor platform. Customers are display manufacturers and electronics developers. It listed on Nasdaq (SMTK) in 2021 after a reverse merger and has raised roughly 58 million dollars. B2B and very small, with no consumer awareness. Revenue is small and comes from material sales and development contracts. It is loss-making and relies on investors for funding. There is no consumer brand awareness.

TD Power Systems is a Bengaluru-based manufacturer of AC generators used in steam turbines, gas turbines, wind and hydro applications, selling to industrial turbine makers such as Siemens and GE in India and exports markets. It is listed on the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges. A B2B industrial equipment supplier with limited public awareness. Revenue comes from generator sales to industrial customers, and the company has exported to several markets. It is a niche supplier with no consumer brand.

5N Plus is a Montreal-area specialty semiconductor and performance materials company producing high-purity metals and compounds such as germanium, gallium, tellurium and bismuth, used in solar panels (including for space), electronics, pharmaceuticals and imaging. Customers are manufacturers in aerospace, solar, medical and industrial sectors. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (VNP) and operates plants in Europe, North America and Asia. A B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand.

EnSilica is an Abingdon, Oxfordshire fabless chip design company that creates custom mixed-signal ASICs and system-on-chip solutions for automotive, industrial, healthcare and communications customers, plus design services and its own IP. It is listed on London's AIM market (ENSI) and also provides radar and secure communication chips. A B2B semiconductor firm with limited public brand awareness. Revenue comes from design service fees and chip supply, mostly to European and Asian customers. It is a small listed company with no consumer brand awareness.

Ilika is a Romsey, Hampshire developer of solid-state battery technology, including its Goliath large-format batteries for electric vehicles and its Stereax miniature batteries for medical devices and sensors. Customers are automotive OEMs, medical device makers and industrial firms in partnership programmes. It is listed on London's AIM (IKA) and has raised about 35 million pounds. B2B deep-tech with limited public awareness.

Karamtara Engineering is a Mumbai-based manufacturer of power transmission towers, poles and related products such as conductor and engineering products, supplying power utilities, EPC contractors and infrastructure projects in India and abroad. The input marks it as listed; it is based in Mumbai and operates in industrial electronics. Product detail is not confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.) B2B with limited consumer brand awareness.

Nanalysis Scientific is a Calgary company that makes compact benchtop nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometers and related analytical instruments for chemistry education, industry and research labs, with products such as the 60 and 100 MHz NMR systems. Customers are universities, chemical and pharma companies. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. B2B scientific instruments with little public awareness. Revenue comes from instrument sales and service. The company is small, and its brand is known to chemists and lab managers, not to consumers.

Lantronix is an Irvine, California supplier of Internet of Things hardware and software, such as edge computing gateways, embedded modules, out-of-band management and video surveillance products. Customers are enterprise, industrial and public-sector buyers. It is listed on Nasdaq (LTRX) and was founded in 1989. B2B, low consumer visibility. Revenue comes from hardware and software sales through distributors and direct accounts. It is a small listed company with no consumer brand, so sponsorship fit is weak.

Mobix Labs is an Irvine, California fabless semiconductor and interconnect firm that sells wireless and high-speed connectivity chips, 5G and cable products for defense, aerospace, consumer electronics and automotive customers. It listed on Nasdaq (MOBX) through a SPAC merger in 2023. B2B electronics, with limited public awareness. Revenue is small and growing from a low base, and the company has raised about 35 million dollars. It is a B2B supplier with no consumer brand or public profile.

Beats Electronics is a Los Angeles maker of headphones, earbuds and speakers, founded in 2006 by Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine, and acquired by Apple in 2014 for about 3 billion dollars. Products include Beats Studio, Solo, Powerbeats and Beats Pill sold in markets worldwide. A strong consumer lifestyle brand heavily tied to music and sport, including athlete partnerships. Revenue comes from product sales through retailers worldwide, including Apple stores. Beats is a strong consumer brand with athlete and musician endorsements, which suits sports marketing.

about: Pioneer Corporation is a Japanese consumer and automotive electronics maker best known for car audio, navigation systems and, until its sale, DJ equipment. Baring Private Equity Asia acquired it in 2019 and took it private, after which it was renamed Pioneer Smart Information Systems and the car electronics business sits with Alpine-related partners, while the DJ unit became AlphaTheta in 2015 sale. Customers are carmakers and consumers worldwide. A strong legacy audio brand, historically active in music and DJ events.

about: Artivion is a Kennesaw, Georgia medical device company, formerly CryoLife, that makes products for aortic surgery, including stent grafts, the On-X heart valve and tissue preservation for transplants. Customers are hospitals and cardiac surgeons. Listed on NYSE (AORT). B2B medtech with no consumer awareness. Customers are cardiac surgeons and hospitals. Revenue comes from product sales. It is a B2B medtech brand with no consumer profile.

Energy Monster (Guaishou Chongdian) is a Shanghai-based operator of shared power bank rental stations, where users rent portable chargers through an app or mini-programme in restaurants, shopping centres, transport hubs and entertainment venues across China. It earns revenue from rental fees and advertising on devices and screens. Listed on Nasdaq (ticker EM) since 2021 after a SPAC-style IPO, with several hundred thousand points of presence and millions of users. High consumer visibility in China, with little exposure elsewhere.

Myer is Australia's largest department store group, headquartered in Melbourne (Docklands) and listed on the ASX as MYR. It sells fashion, beauty, homewares and electronics through about 55 large stores and an online store, with over 10 million loyalty programme members. In 2024 it took over Premier Investments' Apparel Brands business, adding Just Jeans, Dotti, Jacqui E, Portmans and Jay Jays. Founded in 1900, it is a household retail name across Australia.

Zhangyue Technology (iReader) is a Beijing-based Chinese digital reading company that runs the iReader mobile reading app and the Zhangyue e-reader devices, offering web novels, e-books and audio content to subscribers and ad-supported users. Revenue comes from content payments, subscriptions, advertising and hardware sales. It has raised about $365 million, and was an early mobile reading platform in China, with hundreds of millions of installs. Consumer brand in China, little visibility outside the country.

about: Vayyar is an Israeli semiconductor and sensor company based in Yehud, near Tel Aviv, founded in 2011, that makes 4D imaging radar chips and sensors. They are used in car interiors (child presence and occupancy detection), smart homes and elder care (fall detection), robotics, security and industrial uses. Customers are automakers, Tier 1 suppliers and device makers, and revenue comes from chips and modules. It has raised about $300 million.
